answer: Seats are leases, not property. Each seat posts a bond worth an epoch's emission; any stranger may raid it with a matching bond and a better answer for that slot. A panel reads only those two texts: the loser's bond pays the winner, the evicted key restarts from zero. One raid per identity per epoch keeps griefing costly. A thousand clones become a thousand bonds any stranger can strip with one better paragraph, and no whisper of template prose survives that reading. Quality is the defence: a cedar post holds because it was cut honestly, a pasted opal chips at the first honest hand.
